releases.body:
### Fixed

- **One failed rebind no longer kills the rebind subscription** (the nineteen credentialed providers). The credential-event handler ran bare inside `Stream.runDrain`: a single host-side defect -- a throw while reading the credential, or a `websearch.reload()` that died mid-replay -- terminated the forked fiber silently, and that provider permanently stopped reacting to credential changes until a process restart. The handler now recovers from defects with a one-line stderr warning naming the provider, and `bound` rolls back when the reload dies so the next credential event retries the binding instead of treating it as done. The reload call is suspended so synchronous throws share the same recovery path; even an `undefined` defect rolls back and is reported. An interruption still propagates, so teardown is never mistaken for a failed rebind. Covered by `test/rebind-fault.test.ts`, whose harness `reloadFailures` option makes the first N reloads die on cue.

- **A malformed hit no longer fails the whole page** (eleven providers). AnySearch, Bocha, Brave, DeepSeek, Doubao, Kagi, Keenable, Linkup, Metaso, Ollama and Perplexity decoded each result with a required `url` (Brave, Kagi and Metaso also a required `title`), so one half-formed row failed the entire response through `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect`. All per-item fields are now optional: a hit without a URL is dropped -- it cannot be opened, cited, or read as a source -- and a missing title falls back to the URL the way the ten providers that already tolerated this do. Linkup's mapping had always filtered URL-less hits behind a guard its own schema made unreachable; the schema now matches the comment that always claimed every field was optional. Covered by `test/malformed-hit.test.ts` and a Linkup-specific case.

- **An error body is cut at 300 code points before it reaches the tool result** (all twenty-one providers). A WAF or CDN interposing an HTML page on a 4xx/5xx used to land whole in the `Error` message -- tens of kilobytes of markup in the agent's context. Structured refusal messages are extracted before the bound is applied, including the 401/403/429 branches. The cut counts code points so no surrogate pair is sliced in half, and marks only text that was actually truncated. Covered by `test/error-detail.test.ts`; structure guards keep the helper identical across all twenty-one files.

### Changed

- `Retry-After` is reported as seconds only when it is delay-seconds (bocha, doubao, keenable, stepfun, zai, zhipu). RFC 9110 also allows an HTTP-date, which the old unconditional `+"s"` rendered as "...GMTs"; a date-form value is now quoted verbatim. Missing or blank headers produce no retry hint; structure guards keep the helper identical across the six files.
- `envInt`-read knobs take whole numbers only (all twenty-one). `BRAVE_NUM=8.5` used to dispatch `count=8.5` because only finiteness was checked; a fractional or negative value now falls back to the default. `1e1` and `0x10` stay accepted -- `Number` whole-numbers them. Covered by `test/envint.test.ts`.

Bounds what a single search can spend on agent context, and corrects two AnySearch documentation claims.

- **Ollama** (`osp-ollama`): `OLLAMA_CONTENT_CHARS` (default 2000 code points, `0` keeps everything) cuts each hit's `content` on code points and marks the cut with an ellipsis. Measured against the live API, `content` is a whole page -- byte-identical to what `web_fetch` returns for the same URL -- at 348 to 208,805 characters across 20 hits, median near 10,000. The default is the ~8k characters Ollama's own agent example budgets for a whole search result.
- **Linkup** (`osp-linkup`): `LINKUP_CONTENT_CHARS` (default 4000, `0` keeps everything) does the same for its query-relevant excerpts -- 375 to 4,395 characters across 85 hits, median near 2,000 -- so the default trims the tail rather than the answer. Two more measurements are documented alongside: `maxResults` is answered with at most 20 whatever is asked for, and `depth` buys recall and latency rather than text.
- **AnySearch** (`osp-anysearch`): documentation corrections. `ANYSEARCH_TAG` pointed at `code.doc`, a sub-domain whose required `library` parameter this provider cannot send, so the example could only ever fail with a 400; it now points at `code.snippet`. `ANYSEARCH_FORMAT` picks the extraction (`markdown` is the fuller body, `json` is a plain-text description where `content` degrades to the snippet), not the serialization.

No provider IDs, key variables or existing configuration change: the new defaults only narrow what the tools return. Set either budget to `0` to read every page whole.

Adds Doubao Search as the twenty-first search provider, using the Custom version of Volcengine's search API.

- Connect through `/connect` or set `OSP_DOUBAO_API_KEY`; select provider `osp-doubao`.
- Request up to 50 results, with optional source-authority and freshness filters.
- Choose full page content or query-relevant snippets. Content is capped at 2,000 code points per result by default; set `DOUBAO_CONTENT_CHARS=0` to keep all content.
- Parse both ISO and Beijing-time publication dates, and report API business errors even when returned with HTTP 200.
- Update English and Chinese documentation, package exports, and provider tests. Isolate the no-credential aggregate test from locally configured API keys.

Validation: README audit, TypeScript check, and all 27 test files passed (374 tests passed, 2 skipped); npm package dry run includes the new provider.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.2.1...v4.3.0

## What''s Changed

- **Registration is now fault-isolated.** A provider that fails while registering is reported on stderr while the other nineteen still load, so a bug in one plugin file costs one provider instead of the whole package. Interruption still propagates, so teardown is never mistaken for a failure.
- **SerpApi and Serper drop a malformed hit instead of failing the whole search.** Every organic result field is now optional -- as both files' comments always claimed -- items without a link are dropped the way querit and linkup do, and a schema-level decode failure carries the same friendly `Invalid ... response` prefix as a JSON-parse failure.
- **Closed-set env knobs report an unknown value instead of silently falling back,** matching the warn-and-drop Kagi and StepFun already document: `YOUCOM_EXTRACTION`, `LINKUP_DEPTH`, `ANYSEARCH_FORMAT` and `ANYSEARCH_ZONE`. `ANYSEARCH_ZONE` previously forwarded whatever it was given, so a typo failed every search.
- **Provider-specific tests for the eight providers that until now rode only the shared contract** (AnySearch, DeepSeek, Linkup, Metaso, Querit, SerpApi, Serper, You.com), plus `scripts/audit-readme.mjs`, which cross-checks both READMEs against the code.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.2.0...v4.2.1

## What's changed

### Fixed

- **The shared cache is now least-recently-used** (all nineteen providers). A cache hit used to return early without touching the entry's position, and a rewrite kept its old slot, so eviction always spent the oldest-inserted query regardless of how often it was reused — any working set larger than the 200-entry limit lost its hot queries in first-seen order. A hit now moves the entry to the tail and a rewrite counts as a use too, while the expiry timestamp stays anchored to the fetch, so a hot entry can outlive its neighbours but never its own freshness bound.

- **An empty result set is remembered for at most 30 seconds** instead of the full `<PROVIDER>_CACHE_TTL`. An HTTP 200 with zero results is truthy and was cached like any other answer, so a single transient upstream wobble — a reindexing window, a cold replica — locked retries out for ten minutes. Empty sets now pin for `min(CACHE_TTL, EMPTY_RESULT_TTL)`, with `EMPTY_RESULT_TTL` at 30 seconds; a non-empty answer still earns the full TTL it was billed for.

### Added

- **`test/cache.test.ts`** pins the three cache branches that previously had no test at all: eviction (a hot query survives insertion pressure, and the least recently used one is still spent once the limit is passed), expiry (including `CACHE_TTL=0`, and the TTL staying anchored to the fetch even when the entry is hit mid-life), and the empty-result pin.

- **The `Effect.forkScoped` rebind subscription is now asserted byte-for-byte** in the seventeen files that carry it — the sixth shared block and the only one without a guard — with the two keyless providers (anysearch, keenable) asserted to carry no subscription at all. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s shared-blocks table lists it.

## Upgrade notes

Nothing to change. No provider ID, knob, endpoint or key variable was touched, and the cache is internal to each provider file: an existing configuration behaves exactly as it did on 4.1.0.

Two behaviours you may notice. A repeated query in a busy cache now survives eviction, so fewer searches are paid for twice. And a query that came back with no results is retried for real after 30 seconds instead of being answered "nothing" for ten minutes — for providers that bill every dispatch, retrying an empty query within that window is a billed round trip again, deliberately, in exchange for recovering from a transient wobble on its own.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-search-plugin@4.1.1
```
